However, the hypothesis extends this to predict that a controlled annealing intervention will cause segregation, which is not directly tested in the cited work—the evidence only shows the baseline kinetic trapping, not the effect of post-synthesis mobility increase. premises: Low-temperature rapid reduction limits atomic mobility, freezing elements into a random single-phase state
Increased atomic mobility (via annealing or additives) enables segregation and phase separation
Stochastic incorporation of multiple elements governs single-phase HEA formation under restricted mobility
The proposed mechanism applies to solid precursor syntheses with >5 elements at low-to-moderate temperatures
